classification.difficultyReason: Convert six sevenths to recurring decimals and recognise their common cyclic digit pattern.

content.prompt: Express as decimals the fractions between 0 and 1 that have 7 as a denominator. Can you see a pattern?

answer.short:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac17&=0.\dot{1}4285\dot{7}\\\frac27&=0.\dot{2}8571\dot{4}\\\frac37&=0.\dot{4}2857\dot{1}\\\frac47&=0.\dot{5}7142\dot{8}\\\frac57&=0.\dot{7}1428\dot{5}\\\frac67&=0.\dot{8}5714\dot{2}\end{aligned}$$

Each has a six-digit recurring cycle. The cycles are rotations of 142857, with the digits in the same cyclic order.
answer.worked:
Divide each numerator by 7, continuing until a remainder repeats.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac17&=1\div7=0.142857142857\ldots\\\frac17&=0.\dot{1}4285\dot{7}\\\frac27&=2\div7=0.285714285714\ldots\\\frac27&=0.\dot{2}8571\dot{4}\\\frac37&=3\div7=0.428571428571\ldots\\\frac37&=0.\dot{4}2857\dot{1}\\\frac47&=4\div7=0.571428571428\ldots\\\frac47&=0.\dot{5}7142\dot{8}\\\frac57&=5\div7=0.714285714285\ldots\\\frac57&=0.\dot{7}1428\dot{5}\\\frac67&=6\div7=0.857142857142\ldots\\\frac67&=0.\dot{8}5714\dot{2}\end{aligned}$$

For $1\div7$, the successive remainders are $3,2,6,4,5,1$. The remainder 1 returns, so the six digits repeat. Starting with each other numerator gives the same remainder cycle from a different starting point. Thus all six decimals repeat the digits 142857 in the same cyclic order, starting at different digits.
